page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a-nps1.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating with a single thread per core configuration. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core results placing in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the average category, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU benchmarks. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25 percent, although raw memory bandwidth read and write tests for large blocks remain in the average tier. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-level instructions including AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and ADX.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.r7a-nps1.8xlarge is the complete absence of local storage, requiring users to provision external block storage for any persistent data needs. Additionally, while the dedicated physical cores eliminate resource contention, multi-threaded scaling is average rather than top-tier. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density per core makes this instance a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute scaling or local high-speed NVMe drives. This hardware profile is appropriate for memory-intensive applications such as in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and enterprise applications requiring large memory footprints without extreme multi-threaded CPU demands.
